name: 1667-longdecode-llama7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of one a3 node).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine. At this release `worker_use_ray` defaults to False, so TP=1 spawns no Ray actor: there is no second process, no router, and no cache tier outside the node.
architecture: dense decoder-only transformer (LlamaForCausalLM, 32 layers, hidden 4096, intermediate 11008, 32 query heads, multi-head attention -- this checkpoint's config.json carries `num_key_value_heads: null`, which transformers resolves to 32 -- head_dim 128, vocab 32000, rotary position embeddings, SwiGLU feed-forward, 2048-token window). Unquantized fp16: ~13.5 GB of weights.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams 1, warmup 20%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 60 requests with a 3600 s safety cap -- **48** measured requests, each contributing 1023 inter-token gaps. The measured count is `max_requests - warmup` and not `max_requests - warmup - cooldown`, because the declared cooldown never fires: a percent cooldown is sized against `safety_seconds` rather than against the real run, so its boundary sits 3240 s in and a run that ends in about six minutes never reaches it. The warmup, by contrast, is real -- it resolves to a request count, `int(0.2 x 60) = 12`, and 12 is not below `streams: 1`, so request 13 cannot begin until twelve have finished and the cold first request is genuinely excluded. ONE STREAM IS A DECLARED CHOICE AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING: this item is about per-token generation latency, and a single stream is the only operating point at which that quantity is the engine's own decode step rather than a queueing delay behind other requests. A saturating load is a different question at a different operating point, not a re-run of this one.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, `request_format: plain`, `stream: true`, FIXED length by construction: every request is exactly 128 prompt tokens and exactly 1024 output tokens (min=max on both). One shape, repeated, so the run measures a single operating point and nothing else. `plain` hands the prompt to the engine as a raw completion string with no chat template and no role wrapper -- this checkpoint is a base model and ships no chat template, so `plain` is the only honest form. `stream: true` is what makes the backend stamp a timing on every token rather than only on the final output, and without it `inter_token_latency_ms` is not measurable. Sampling is greedy (`temperature: 0.0`) as a control: it pins the emitted token sequence, so a run traverses one KV path and one code path. `ignore_eos` is forced whenever `max_tokens` is set, so every request emits exactly 1024 tokens and the step counts are identical run to run. WIRE LENGTH IS DECLARED LENGTH: the generator encodes a Faker paragraph, truncates to 128 ids and decodes with `skip_special_tokens=True`; that encode had prepended a BOS, so the decoded string carries 127 content tokens and vLLM re-adds a BOS when it tokenizes, and the two cancel.
purpose: A single-user long-form text generator on one 7B model and one GPU, writing 1024 streamed tokens per short prompt.
launch:
# A November 2023 vLLM serving a 7B LLaMA on one card to a single stream, decoding a long
# completion from a short prompt. Nothing here is tuned and there is no tuned.yaml.
#
# ERA NOTE, so that nothing below is read as an omission: this engine predates chunked prefill,
# prefix caching, speculative decoding and the V1 engine. None of those knobs exist in its
# argument parser, and passing one would fail to launch rather than be ignored.

# The ungated LLaMA-1 7B; fp16, ~13.5 GB. NOT in the local cache -- it downloads on first run.
model: huggyllama/llama-7b

# One card. A 7B in fp16 fits one H100 with room to spare. At TP=1 this engine keeps the worker
# in-process: `worker_use_ray` defaults to False, so there is no Ray actor and no router.
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# `auto` reads torch_dtype: float16 off this checkpoint, so `auto` and float16 are the same thing
# here; written out so a change of default cannot silently move the activation arithmetic.
dtype: float16

# The workload is 128 prompt + 1024 generated = 1152 tokens of context. 2048 is this checkpoint's
# own `max_position_embeddings` and the largest value it will accept.
max-model-len: 2048

# This engine's own default, written out so a change of default cannot move the KV cache size.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# This engine's own default: 4 GiB of pinned host memory for preemption swap. Nothing in this
# workload should ever swap -- one stream of 1152 tokens against tens of GB of KV.
swap-space: 4

# --- DELIBERATELY ABSENT:
#   max-num-seqs / max-num-batched-tokens -- left at this engine's defaults (max_num_seqs 256;
#                     max_num_batched_tokens unset, which this engine's scheduler resolves to
#                     max(max_model_len, 2048) = 2048) so the running batch follows the offered
#                     load, which the load profile in scenario.json is what fixes.
#   quantization   -- the checkpoint is unquantized fp16 and nothing overrides it.
#   kv-cache-dtype -- does not exist at this release.
#   seed           -- the sampler is greedy (temperature 0.0 in scenario.json), so there is
#                     nothing for a seed to decide.
